summary: Introductory kickoff for Moonridge Systems' Redwood Inference onboarding. Covered integration options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), network and security requirements, runbook and rollout plan, success metrics (latency, cost per 1k tokens, availability), and an initial staging test plan. Agreed on pilot scope: 2-week sandbox, end-to-end benchmark, and deliver security pack + access. Action items and dates captured.
topics: Current infra and constraints (K8s, VPC, edge VPN)
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
Runbook: rollout phases, canary policy, fallbacks
Benchmarks: latency SLOs and token cost targets
Pilot plan: timelines, success criteria, stakeholders
transcript: 00:00 Jordan Li: Hey everyone, thanks for getting on at the end of the year, appreciate it. Happy New Year in advance. 00:08 Liam O'Connor: Thanks Jordan, likewise. We'll try to keep this short and actionable. 00:12 Sofia Martinez: Quick intro - I'm Sofia, CSM, I'll be your main point for onboarding and runbook ops. 00:20 Priya Nambiar: Hi, Priya, Head of ML here. We're driving the inference integration. 00:25 Ethan Cole: Ethan from Redwood's SE team, I'll handle the technical side — runtimes, perf. 00:30 Carlos Vega: Carlos, platform eng. We manage their k8s clusters and the VPCs. 00:40 Aisha Rahman: Aisha, security. We'll need to validate encryption and audit trails. 00:45 Jordan Li: Great. Agenda: confirm constraints, pick deployment mode, map out pilot, and list action items. 00:55 Liam O'Connor: Our main goals: sub-150ms 95th perc latency for chat endpoints, predictable monthly cost, and no PHI leakage. Timeline: pilot in Jan, prod by March if all goes well. 01:10 Priya Nambiar: For models we'll start with a 13B open model. We'll test chat and embedding flows. 01:18 Ethan Cole: That maps well to Redwood's profiles — we can run the initial bench on Hosted to move quickly, then switch to Dedicated or Private if you need data isolation. 01:28 Carlos Vega: We prefer private deployment (VPC) because of compliance, but we can do a staging hosted run to validate prompts. Concern is egress and peering costs. 01:40 Sofia Martinez: Totally common. For many customers we do a two-step: sandbox on Hosted API, then Dedicated/Dedicated-in-VPC for prod. We can document cost delta. 01:52 Aisha Rahman: Security checklist: SSO (SAML), audit logs retention 1 year, KMS integration, and SOC2 attestation evidence. We also need DB redaction patterns and a data retention policy. 02:06 Jordan Li: Redwood supports SAML SSO, audit logs, and has KMS hooks. We'll send the compliance pack after. Note: sometimes transcriptions in our docs call it Redwood Dedicted, sorry -- means Dedicated. 02:20 Priya Nambiar: (laughs) Noted. On perf: how do you handle KV cache warm-up and long-context chat? 02:28 Ethan Cole: The runtime uses continuous batching and efficient KV cache management. For long-context we recommend keeping prefix caching and pinning model versions. We'll demo KV caching in the tech check. 02:42 Carlos Vega: About autoscaling — do you offer autoscaling in the private deploy, or is that only on Dedicated? 02:49 Ethan Cole: Both Dedicated and Private can be configured with autoscale policies. Private requires you to enable autoscaling agent and we help tune those policies. 02:58 Liam O'Connor: If we go Private, network setup is a potential blocker. We have strict egress rules and a private peering team. 03:05 Sofia Martinez: We'll coordinate the network runbook with your platform folks. Typical items: VPN/peering, route tables, and firewall ports for heartbeat. 03:15 Aisha Rahman: Encryption at rest and in transit — we require HSM-backed keys for prod. Does Redwood integrate with customer KMS/HSM? 03:24 Jordan Li: Yes — KMS integrations supported. For HSM we have a partner flow, and we'll capture steps in the compliance doc. 03:34 Priya Nambiar: For success criteria, here are ours: 1) 95p latency <150ms for up to 500 RPS in steady state, 2) token cost < $0.015 per 1k tokens for basic completions, 3) zero data exfil incidents in pilot. 03:52 Ethan Cole: We'll baseline the 95p in our benchmark run. One note: latency vs cost is a tradeoff — quantization and batching reduces cost but can increase per-token latency in some cases. 04:05 Carlos Vega: Are there recommended quantization settings? Our models are 13B with mixed precision currently. 04:13 Ethan Cole: We'll recommend a quant profile — often 4-bit for throughput workloads, and dynamic batch sizing. We'll include a recommended config for your test. 04:25 Priya Nambiar: How do we measure token accounting? We need transparency in the console. 04:30 Sofia Martinez: Redwood Console gives token-level breakdowns and per-route dashboards. We'll give you access to a demo org to view sample traces. 04:41 Liam O'Connor: On roles — who will be our Redwood contacts day-to-day? 04:45 Sofia Martinez: I'll be your primary CSM for the pilot and runbook ops. Ethan will be SE lead for tech checks. Jordan is AE for contract and escalation. 04:55 Priya Nambiar: Great. Pilot scope specifics? 05:00 Jordan Li: Proposal: two-week sandbox starting Jan 8. Goals: integrate basic API calls, run synthetic benchmark, run one end-to-end scenario with redacted production data, and provide a performance report. 05:16 Carlos Vega: For the end-to-end we'll need a staging VPC peering and service account with least privilege. We'll also need a sample prompt set. 05:25 Sofia Martinez: We'll provide a starter prompt set and a sample benchmark harness. 05:30 Aisha Rahman: Will the sandbox store logs with PII? We need to ensure redaction prior to any external persistence. 05:36 Ethan Cole: Sandbox can be configured with ephemeral logs and with prefix/KV caching disabled if you want zero persisted state. We'll outline options. 05:47 Priya Nambiar: Are there known incompatibilities with our infra? We're on k8s 1.26 and use Istio for mesh. 05:55 Ethan Cole: No blockers — Redwood Private supports common service meshes; we'll validate sidecar traffic rules. 06:04 Carlos Vega: How do we run canary rollouts? We need automatic fallback if latency crosses threshold. 06:11 Sofia Martinez: Redwood's rollout supports canary and automatic fallback by policy — we can set thresholds on p95 latency or error rate to roll back. 06:21 Liam O'Connor: Pricing and contract cadence: Jordan? 06:24 Jordan Li: For pilot we can provide a time-bound eval with credits. Post-pilot, depending on Dedicated vs Private we'll provide a reserved capacity estimate. We'll send a pricing appendix. 06:36 Priya Nambiar: Integration tasks — who creates the networking tickets? 06:40 Carlos Vega: I'll open tickets with our infra and share the VPC peering contact. 06:44 Sofia Martinez: Perfect — we'll need the peer IP ranges and NAT details. 06:50 Priya Nambiar: Any concerns about model versioning and rollbacks? We need stable model pins for reproducibility. 06:57 Ethan Cole: Models can be pinned per-route and we support snapshot rollouts so you can revert quickly. 07:05 Aisha Rahman: Audit logs — what's the retention and export options? We need to push logs to our SIEM. 07:12 Jordan Li: Audit logs can be exported via secure syslog or S3, retention configurable. We'll include SIEM connector docs. 07:21 Liam O'Connor: Ok let's talk calendar: we'll aim for a tech-check with Ethan and Carlos next Tuesday, Jan 6, 10am UTC. Does that work? 07:30 Carlos Vega: Works for me. 07:32 Ethan Cole: I'm available. 07:33 Sofia Martinez: I'll schedule and include runbook draft. 07:37 Priya Nambiar: Final question — any gotchas for large prompt histories and token costs? 07:44 Ethan Cole: Keep history trimming and prefix caching. We'll show tooling to estimate token burn. 07:52 Jordan Li: Good. Let's recap action items and next steps now. 08:00 Sofia Martinez: Recap — 1) Redwood to send compliance pack (SOC2 + SSO + KMS integration steps) — Owner: Jordan/Sofia — Due: 2027-01-03. 08:15 2) Moonridge to open networking ticket and share peering details — Owner: Carlos — Due: 2027-01-04. 08:25 3) Schedule tech-check (Ethan + Carlos) — Owner: Sofia — Due: 2027-01-03. 08:35 4) Provide sample prompt set and benchmark harness — Owner: Redwood (Sofia/Ethan) — Due: 2027-01-05. 08:50 5) Confirm pilot start date and sign MSA or pilot terms — Owner: Jordan/Liam — Due: 2027-01-06. 09:05 Liam O'Connor: All good, appreciate the clarity. 09:10 Jordan Li: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with meeting notes and the compliance pack. Happy holidays. 09:15 [Recording ends]
